newsitem.title: USA: US House panel approves $85 bln tax cut bill.
newsitem.headline: US House panel approves $85 bln tax cut bill.

text.p: The U.S. House tax-writing committee on Friday approved a bill that would cut taxes by a net $85 billion over five years and, if enacted, would give Americans the first major tax cut in 16 years.

The House Ways and Means Committee voted along party lines 22 to 16 to approve Republican legislation that included a child tax credit, education tax initiatives, and a reduction in the capital gains tax.
Committee chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, who crafted the legislation that will now go to the House floor for a vote, said, "I think the House will pass this bill."
The Clinton administration has voiced concerns about the bill, especially the way the education tax initiatives are structured.
Don Lubick, acting Treasury Assistant Secretary for tax policy, said during the committee meeting, "We have serious concerns, as you know, with the chairman's (bill)."

The legislation would also increase taxes by about $46 billion with various measures, including an extension of the airline ticket tax and elimination of federal subsidies to ethanol producers. But the panel rejected a proposal to also increase the federal tax on cigarettes.
